title: Caveat: not by free will or meritorious works
source_text: LI. Quod autem hic sedulo cavendum putant Reformati illud est, ne putetur homo viribus naturalibus liberi arbitrii, posse se quadantenus ad gratiam praeparare, aut ope-ribus quibuscunque, etiam gratiae auxilio factis, remissionem peccatorum, & eorum ablutionem, aut Spiritus Sancti donum quoquomodo promereri: quo tendere putant illa quae Pontificii docent de praeparationibus, & dispositionibus variis ad gratiam justi-ficantem, & sanctificantem. Nec alio animo & fine disputant contra Pontificios, & impugnant dispositiones seu praeparationes.
pass_a_gloss: But what the Reformed think must here be carefully guarded against is this: lest it be thought that a man by the natural powers of free will can in some measure prepare himself for grace, or by any works whatsoever, even those done with the help of grace, in any way merit the remission of sins and their washing, or the gift of the Holy Spirit—to which they think those things tend which the Papists teach about preparations and various dispositions to justifying and sanctifying grace. Nor with any other mind and end do they dispute against the Papists and impugn dispositions or preparations.
pass_b_english: Reformed carefully deny that natural free will can prepare for grace, or that any works—even grace-aided—merit remission or the Spirit.
That is what they fight when opposing Roman preparation-talk.
